name: Yahtzee

setup.text: Put the shaker, five dice and score cards where everyone can reach them.
Write your name on a score card, in turn order (one column each).
Roll a die to see who starts. Play continues clockwise.

turn.summary: Roll the five dice up to three times, then fill in exactly one empty box.
steps: First roll: roll all five dice. If you already have the combination you want, score it now.
Second roll: set aside the dice you want to keep and re-roll the rest, or re-roll them all.
Third roll: again re-roll any or all dice, including ones you set aside before. You must score after this roll.
Write one score in one empty box in your column. If nothing fits, you must write a zero in one empty box.

end: The game ends after 13 rounds, when every box on every score card is filled. The highest grand total wins.

scoring.text: Upper section: for Aces to Sixes, add up only the dice showing that number.
Bonus: 35 points if your upper section reaches the bonus line (63, which is three of each number).
3 of a Kind and 4 of a Kind: score the total of all five dice.
Full House (3 of a kind plus a pair): 25. Small Straight (4 in a row): 30. Large Straight (5 in a row): 40.
YAHTZEE (5 of a kind): 50. Chance: total of all five dice, any roll.
Extra YAHTZEE: mark the YAHTZEE bonus box (100 points) and also fill one empty box as normal.

missed.text: You must fill in one box every turn, and a filled box cannot be used again.
You can fill boxes in any order, but you never get to skip a turn.
A bonus YAHTZEE needs a score in the YAHTZEE box that is not zero. If you already scored zero there, no 100 points.
For an extra YAHTZEE, fill the matching upper box first. If that is full, use 3 or 4 of a Kind. If those are full, use Chance or take any combination box at its normal score (Full House is 25).
A single matching die in the upper section is better than a zero.

unverified: The text says 'over 63' for the bonus, but also says three of each number reaches it, which totals exactly 63. Entry treats 63 as enough.
The 2+ players figure is the only count given; the maximum of 6 is a working limit, not stated.
